title: BTC to ETH: Native Bitcoin vs Wrapped Bitcoin — What Are You Actually Sending?
keyQuestions: Is WBTC the same as BTC?
Why can BTC and WBTC have almost the same dollar value?
How can I tell whether I own BTC or WBTC?
Can I send WBTC directly to a Bitcoin address?
Does WBTC always exist on Ethereum?
Do I have to convert BTC to WBTC before exchanging BTC for ETH?
What if the exchange asks for BTC but my wallet contains WBTC?
quickSteps: Identify the exact Bitcoin-related asset in your wallet instead of relying on its icon or market value.
Confirm the blockchain where that balance exists and determine whether it is a native coin or a token.
Match native BTC to the Bitcoin-side requirement of the BTC to ETH route before preparing any transfer.
Verify the ETH network and receiving wallet independently from the Bitcoin source side.
Stop if the asset identity or network does not match, and choose an explicit conversion path rather than testing an incompatible transfer.

issueRouting.start: What should you do if your wallet shows Bitcoin-related value but you are not sure whether it can fund a BTC to ETH swap?

branches.if: The wallet shows native BTC on the Bitcoin network.
then: Confirm that the BTC to ETH route expects native BTC.
Verify the current Bitcoin-side deposit requirement before preparing the transfer.
Check the ETH payout network and receiving address separately.

branches.if: The wallet shows WBTC or another Bitcoin-linked token.
then: Identify the exact network where the token exists.
Do not substitute it for a native BTC deposit unless the route explicitly supports that asset and network.
Use a supported conversion path if native BTC is required.

branches.if: The wallet interface does not make the asset or network clear.
then: Open the asset details and check the ticker, network, and native-or-token status.
Do not rely on the wallet brand, Bitcoin logo, or fiat price to identify the asset.
Stop before sending until the asset identity matches the receiving requirement.

riskNotes: Similar market value does not make BTC and WBTC interchangeable at the blockchain level.
WBTC should not be sent to a native Bitcoin deposit as a normal token transfer.
WBTC is available on multiple networks, so the token name alone does not identify the settlement network.
A multichain wallet can display native BTC and wrapped Bitcoin in the same interface without combining them into one spendable balance.
Wrapping BTC is not automatically required before a BTC to ETH swap when the selected route accepts native BTC directly.
An incompatible test transfer is still an incompatible transfer, even when the amount is small.
